title: Kustomize Declarative Configuration Management
summary: Master template-free Kubernetes configuration management using Kustomize, base and multi-environment overlays, strategic merge patches, JSON 6902 patches, and configMapGenerator hash suffixes.
learningObjectives: Design clean Base and Multi-Environment Overlay directory structures to maintain DRY Kubernetes manifests.
Apply Strategic Merge Patches and JSON 6902 Patches to customize replicas, resources, and environment variables across environments.
Leverage configMapGenerator and secretGenerator with content-hashed suffixes to drive automated zero-downtime rolling updates.

curriculumModules.title: Kustomize Philosophy, Base & Overlay Composition
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kustomize introduces template-free configuration customization natively integrated into kubectl (-k). The base layer contains pure, valid Kubernetes manifests representing standard infrastructure. Overlays reference the base (resources: [../../base]) and apply environment-specific transforms such as namePrefix, namespace, commonLabels, and replica overrides.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Maintain a canonical base/ directory per microservice with overlays/staging/ and overlays/production/ managed via GitOps repositories to eliminate template syntax errors and YAML drift.

curriculumModules.title: Strategic Merge Patches & JSON 6902 Transformations
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kustomize offers two patching mechanisms: Strategic Merge Patches (SMP), which merge partial YAML snippets using Kubernetes schema merge keys, and RFC 6902 JSON Patches, which perform explicit operations (add, replace, remove) targeted at specific JSONPointer paths (/spec/replicas).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use Strategic Merge Patches for clean additions of environment variables or resource limits, and use JSON 6902 patches when targeting specific items in unkeyed arrays.

curriculumModules.title: ConfigMap / Secret Generators & Rollout Synchronization
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: configMapGenerator and secretGenerator generate resources from files or literals and append a deterministic 10-character content hash to their names. When configuration changes, the hash changes, updating the PodTemplateSpec and triggering an automatic Kubernetes rolling update without manual pod deletion.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Never deploy static ConfigMap names without versioning; leverage Kustomize generators to guarantee that configuration updates trigger immediate, zero-downtime rollouts.

labs.title: Multi-Environment Overlay Architecture & Strategic Merge Patches
labs.scenario: A payments microservice needs separate configurations for staging and production without template duplication. Create a base directory with deployment and service manifests, construct a production overlay that applies namePrefix, namespace 'production', commonLabels, and a strategic merge patch setting replicas to 3, and deploy using kubectl apply -k.
labs.productionContext: Kustomize overlays allow platform teams to promote workloads across dev, staging, and production clusters with strict GitOps traceability and zero template engine overhead.
objectives: Create base Kubernetes manifests and base kustomization.yaml
Construct production overlay with namespace, namePrefix, and replica patch
Render composite manifests using kustomize build overlays/production
Deploy the production overlay with kubectl apply -k overlays/production

steps.title: Scaffold Base Infrastructure
steps.commandHint:
mkdir -p base && echo -e "apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments-api
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payments-api
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine" > base/deployment.yaml && echo -e "resources:
- deployment.yaml" > base/kustomization.yaml

steps.title: Create Production Overlay with Strategic Patch
steps.instruction: Create `overlays/production/` with a patch scaling replicas to 3 and setting namespace to `production`.
steps.commandHint:
mkdir -p overlays/production && echo -e "resources:
- ../../base
namespace: production
namePrefix: prod-
commonLabels:
  env: production
patchesStrategicMerge:
- patch-replicas.yaml" > overlays/production/kustomization.yaml && echo -e "apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments-api
spec:
  replicas: 3" > overlays/production/patch-replicas.yaml

steps.title: Build and Inspect Rendered Output
steps.instruction: Render the composite production manifests using `kustomize build overlays/production`.

steps.title: Apply Overlay to Cluster
steps.instruction: Deploy the rendered production workload using `kubectl apply -k overlays/production`.

labs.title: ConfigMap Generators, Secret Generators & Rollout Synchronization
labs.scenario: To prevent stale configuration bugs, application configuration must be injected via Kustomize configMapGenerator and secretGenerator. Create a kustomization file defining configMapGenerator for 'api-config' with environment variables and secretGenerator for 'api-secrets', build with kustomize, and apply with kubectl apply -k.
labs.productionContext: Generated ConfigMaps with SHA-256 hash suffixes prevent race conditions during updates and guarantee that pods always bind to the exact configuration version they were deployed with.
objectives: Create kustomization with configMapGenerator and secretGenerator
Inspect generated content-hash resource names with kustomize build
Apply generators to cluster using kubectl apply -k .
Verify ConfigMap with content-hash suffix is created in cluster

steps.title: Configure ConfigMap and Secret Generators
steps.commandHint:
echo -e "apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
configMapGenerator:
- name: api-config
  literals:
  - ENV=production
  - LOG_LEVEL=info
secretGenerator:
- name: api-secrets
  literals:
  - DB_PASSWORD=SuperSecretPass123!" > kustomization.yaml

steps.title: Render Generated Manifests with Content Hashes
steps.instruction: Verify that `api-config` and `api-secrets` receive unique 10-character hash suffixes using `kustomize build .`.

steps.title: Deploy Generated Resources
steps.instruction: Apply the generated configuration to the cluster with `kubectl apply -k .`.

steps.title: Inspect ConfigMap in Cluster
steps.instruction: Verify the generated ConfigMap exists using `kubectl get configmap api-config-7m8f9b2c4k`.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Kustomize configMapGenerator solve the problem of pods failing to reload modified ConfigMap contents?
options: (Recommended) It appends a content hash suffix to the ConfigMap name and updates referencing Pod templates, triggering an automatic Kubernetes rolling restart upon configuration changes.
It establishes an in-memory gRPC watcher that hot-reloads running application memory.
It forces the kubelet daemon to execute a hard node reboot.
It automatically writes configuration updates directly into the host /etc/kubernetes/manifests folder.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Because Kubernetes Deployments only trigger a rolling update when the PodTemplateSpec changes, appending a deterministic content-hash suffix to generated ConfigMaps (e.g. app-config-7m8f9b2c4k) guarantees that any change in data changes the Pod spec name, triggering an atomic zero-downtime rollout.

assessmentQuestions.question: In Kustomize overlay composition, what is the key difference between a Strategic Merge Patch and a JSON 6902 patch?
options: (Recommended) Strategic Merge Patches use standard Kubernetes YAML schema keys to merge maps and lists, whereas JSON 6902 patches specify exact operations (add, replace, remove) targeted by JSONPointer paths.
JSON 6902 patches can only be applied to Secrets, while Strategic Merge Patches only work on Services.
Strategic Merge Patches require an external Helm Tiller server to execute.
JSON 6902 patches recompile the entire Linux kernel inside the target container.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Strategic Merge Patching relies on Kubernetes API schema semantics (like patchStrategy and patchMergeKey on lists) to merge partial YAML manifests. In contrast, RFC 6902 JSON Patching provides imperative array-based operations (add, remove, replace, move, copy, test) targeting precise JSONPointer paths.
